blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Handyman Cost in Torquay? A Complete 2026 Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover how much a handyman costs in Torquay in 2026. We break down real pricing for common home repairs, maintenance tasks and property improvements on the Surf Coast.
body: If you are a Torquay homeowner wondering what a handyman costs in 2026, you are not alone. The Surf Coast region has seen steady growth, with property values rising and homeowners increasingly turning to professional handyman services rather than attempting complex DIY projects. In Torquay, typical handyman hourly rates range from $65 to $95 per hour, depending on the complexity of the job and the materials required. At Fix Up Look Sharp, we have been servicing Torquay, Armstrong Creek and the wider Geelong region for over ten years, and we understand that transparent pricing matters to every customer. This guide breaks down real costs for common handyman tasks in the Torquay area, factoring in local labour rates, Surf Coast building considerations and the unique challenges of maintaining homes in a coastal environment where salt air and wind can accelerate wear on exterior surfaces and fixtures.

One of the most common handyman requests in Torquay is door and window repairs. The coastal climate means timber frames and sills are particularly vulnerable to moisture ingress and warping. Replacing a standard interior door in Torquay typically costs between $150 and $300, including the door, hardware and installation labour. For exterior doors, especially those exposed to the harsh Surf Coast winds, expect to pay $300 to $600 for supply and install. Window repairs vary significantly, a simple seal replacement might cost $80 to $120, while a full window frame repair in a Torquay beach house could run $400 or more. Fix Up Look Sharp carries common door and window hardware on our work vehicles, which means many Torquay jobs can be completed in a single visit without waiting for parts to be ordered. We also stock coastal-rated weatherstripping and seals that are designed to withstand the salt air conditions common throughout the Surf Coast region.

Furniture assembly and mounting services are increasingly popular in Torquay, particularly among the growing number of young families settling in Armstrong Creek and surrounding suburbs. Flat-pack furniture from retailers like IKEA and Fantastic Furniture is affordable, but the assembly process can be frustrating and time-consuming. A professional furniture assembly service in Torquay typically charges $80 to $150 for a standard wardrobe or bed frame, and $120 to $250 for more complex items like entertainment units or outdoor setting assembly. Wall mounting for TVs is another frequent request, we charge $100 to $180 to securely mount a TV to a plasterboard or brick wall, including all necessary brackets and fixings. For Torquay homes with brick veneer construction, we use specialised masonry anchors to ensure a safe, permanent installation that meets Australian standards. Our furniture assembly service covers all major brands and we arrive with the tools and fixings needed to get the job done efficiently.

Painting and plastering represent a significant portion of handyman work across the Surf Coast. Whether you are refreshing a rental property between tenants or updating your Torquay home's interior, professional painting delivers the best return on investment. Interior painting in Torquay typically costs $35 to $55 per square metre, including preparation, two coats and clean-up. For a standard bedroom, expect to pay $800 to $1,500 depending on wall condition and colour complexity. Exterior painting in coastal Torquay requires careful surface preparation due to salt air exposure, budget $45 to $70 per square metre for weatherboard or rendered surfaces. Patching and plastering minor wall damage in Torquay homes ranges from $80 to $200 per repair, making it an affordable way to maintain your property's appearance and value. Fix Up Look Sharp uses marine-grade exterior paints on all outdoor work in Torquay, ensuring your paintwork lasts longer in the challenging coastal environment.

Decking and fencing are particularly important in Torquay, where outdoor living is a year-round priority and coastal weather takes a toll on timber structures. Replacing damaged deck boards in Torquay typically costs $40 to $65 per square metre for treated pine, or $70 to $110 per square metre for premium hardwood like spotted gum. A full deck restoration including sanding, oiling and replacing damaged boards usually runs $1,200 to $3,000 depending on deck size. For fencing, a standard Colorbond fence replacement in Torquay costs approximately $75 to $120 per linear metre installed, while timber paling fences run $60 to $95 per linear metre. The Surf Coast's exposure to strong southerly winds means fences in Torquay need proper post-concreting and bracing, which Fix Up Look Sharp always includes as standard practice. We recommend Torquay homeowners inspect their outdoor timber structures at least twice a year, particularly before the harsh summer season begins.

Gutter cleaning and general property maintenance are essential in Torquay, where the combination of coastal winds, overhanging trees and seasonal leaf fall can quickly block gutters and cause water damage. A professional gutter clean in Torquay typically costs $150 to $300 for a standard single-storey home, and $250 to $450 for a two-storey property. Given the Surf Coast's heavy winter rainfall, having clean gutters is critical for preventing fascia rot and foundation damage. Beyond gutters, regular handyman maintenance in Torquay includes checking and tightening outdoor fixtures, repainting weather-exposed surfaces and addressing minor repairs before they become expensive problems. We recommend Torquay homeowners schedule a comprehensive maintenance check every six months, ideally before the autumn and spring seasons when the Surf Coast weather is most demanding on residential properties.

When budgeting for handyman services in Torquay, it is important to consider the value of combining multiple small jobs into a single visit. Many Torquay homeowners save significantly by creating a maintenance list and having a handyman complete everything in one appointment. At Fix Up Look Sharp, we offer discounted rates for multi-task visits across Torquay and Armstrong Creek, meaning you pay for the call-out once and get multiple repairs handled efficiently. Always request a written quote before any work begins, and ensure your handyman holds current public liability insurance to protect you and your Torquay property. For an accurate, no-obligation quote on your specific handyman needs in Torquay, contact Fix Up Look Sharp on 0415 451 675 or visit our website for more information about our services across the Surf Coast and greater Geelong region.

blogPosts.title: Torquay Home Maintenance Checklist: What to Fix Before Summer on the Surf Coast
blogPosts.excerpt: Get your Torquay home ready for summer with our comprehensive Surf Coast maintenance checklist. From gutter cleaning to deck care, protect your property from harsh coastal conditions.
body: Living in Torquay means enjoying world-class beaches and a vibrant outdoor lifestyle, but it also means your home faces some of Victoria's harshest coastal conditions. Before summer arrives on the Surf Coast, it is essential to go through a comprehensive home maintenance checklist to protect your property from intense UV exposure, salt-laden winds and occasional storms that characterise the region. At Fix Up Look Sharp, we have helped hundreds of Torquay and Armstrong Creek homeowners prepare their properties for the summer season, and we have seen firsthand how a little preventive maintenance can save thousands in costly repairs. This checklist covers the most critical maintenance tasks for Torquay homes, from exterior weatherproofing to indoor comfort upgrades that will keep your family cool and your energy bills manageable throughout the peak summer months on the Surf Coast.

The exterior of your Torquay home is the first line of defence against the harsh Surf Coast summer. Start by inspecting all exterior timber surfaces, including door frames, window sills, deck boards and fence panels. The combination of salt air and UV radiation in Torquay causes timber to dry, crack and grey far more rapidly than homes further inland. Look for signs of rot, particularly around ground-contact areas and joints where water can pool. Any damaged timber should be replaced or treated before summer accelerates the deterioration. Check your home's exterior paintwork for bubbling, peeling or chalky residue, all signs that the coating has failed and your substrate is exposed. A fresh coat of quality exterior paint or timber oil applied in early spring will provide critical UV protection throughout the Torquay summer. Do not forget to inspect and treat any exposed screws or fasteners to prevent rust staining on your home's exterior surfaces.

Gutter cleaning is arguably the most important pre-summer maintenance task for Torquay homeowners. The Surf Coast experiences significant autumn leaf fall, and by early spring, gutters can be completely blocked with accumulated debris. Blocked gutters in Torquay can cause fascia board rot, water damage to eaves and even foundation problems during heavy summer storms. A thorough gutter clean should include removing all debris, flushing downpipes to ensure clear water flow and checking that all gutter brackets are secure and properly angled toward downpipes. While you are up there, inspect the condition of your fascia boards and soffits for any signs of water damage, rot or pest activity. Torquay homes near reserve areas or with large gum trees may need more frequent gutter maintenance, consider scheduling cleans every three to four months during peak leaf-drop periods. Fix Up Look Sharp offers affordable gutter cleaning packages for Torquay and Armstrong Creek residents.

Summer in Torquay brings longer days and more time outdoors, making deck maintenance a priority for most homeowners. Begin by giving your deck a thorough clean using a specialised deck cleaner to remove accumulated dirt, mould and any salt residue from the winter months. Inspect every board for signs of warping, splitting or rot, paying particular attention to areas near posts and where boards meet the house. Replace any damaged boards before they become safety hazards or allow water to penetrate the substructure. Once cleaned and repaired, apply a quality timber oil or stain to protect against UV damage and moisture. In Torquay's coastal environment, we recommend re-oiling decks at least once annually, with a light maintenance coat every six months for heavily exposed areas. A well-maintained deck not only looks fantastic for summer entertaining but also adds significant value to your Torquay property.

Interior preparation for a Torquay summer focuses on comfort and efficiency. Check all window and door seals for gaps that allow hot air to infiltrate your home. Replacing worn weatherstripping is an inexpensive fix that can noticeably reduce cooling costs during Torquay's warmest days. Test all ceiling fans to ensure they are operating correctly and rotating in the right direction, clockwise in summer to create a cooling downdraft. Consider having your home's interior painted in lighter colours to reflect heat and brighten living spaces. If you have been putting off that room refresh, spring is the ideal time to get it done before the busy summer season. Check smoke alarms and replace batteries as needed, a critical safety task that is easy to overlook. For Torquay rental property owners, pre-summer maintenance ensures your property is tenant-ready and complies with Victorian rental safety standards.

Outdoor areas beyond the deck need attention too. Inspect your fence line for any panels that have been loosened by winter storms, Torquay's exposed coastal position means fences cop a beating from strong winds, particularly along the western and southern boundaries. Repair or replace any damaged Colorbond or timber fence sections before summer storms cause further damage. Check outdoor lighting to ensure all fixtures are working and properly aimed for safety and security during the longer summer evenings. Inspect your clothesline, letterbox, house numbers and any exterior fixtures for rust or damage. These small items may seem insignificant, but they contribute to your home's overall presentation and can be quick fixes for a professional handyman. Oil any sticky hinges, tighten loose screws and lubricate sliding door tracks to keep everything operating smoothly throughout the Torquay summer.

Do not forget the less obvious maintenance tasks that can prevent expensive emergencies. Check your hot water system for any signs of leaking or reduced performance, Torquay's hard water can accelerate mineral buildup in elements and valves. Inspect bathroom and kitchen silicone seals for mould or gaps that could allow water damage behind walls or under floors. Test your home's RCD safety switches and circuit breakers to ensure they are functioning correctly. If your Torquay home has a water tank, clean the first-flush diverter and check that all connections are secure before the summer storm season. Finally, create a basic emergency kit with torches, batteries and a portable phone charger, Torquay can experience power outages during severe weather events. By working through this checklist, Torquay homeowners can enjoy peace of mind knowing their property is protected and ready for whatever the Surf Coast summer brings.

blogPosts.title: Best Timber for Fencing in Torquay: Surf Coast Weather Considerations
blogPosts.excerpt: Choosing the right timber for your Torquay fence? We compare treated pine, hardwood, ironbark and Colorbond for Surf Coast conditions, including costs, durability and maintenance tips.
body: Choosing the right timber for your fencing project in Torquay is more important than many homeowners realise. The Surf Coast's unique combination of salt-laden coastal winds, intense UV exposure, high rainfall and occasional severe storms creates a demanding environment that can destroy poorly chosen fencing materials within just a few years. At Fix Up Look Sharp, we have installed and repaired countless fences across Torquay, Armstrong Creek, Anglesea and the wider Geelong region, and we have developed clear preferences for timber species that stand up to the local conditions. This comprehensive guide will help Torquay homeowners understand which timber options offer the best balance of durability, appearance and value for fencing in the Surf Coast region, along with practical maintenance tips to maximise the lifespan of your investment.

Treated pine remains the most popular fencing material in Torquay, and for good reason, it offers an excellent combination of affordability, availability and durability when properly maintained. Australian-standard treated pine (H3 rated for above-ground use, H4 for in-ground posts) has been pressure-treated with preservatives that protect against termites, fungal decay and borers, all of which are active in the Torquay area. A standard treated pine paling fence in Torquay typically costs $60 to $95 per linear metre installed, making it the most budget-friendly option for most residential properties. However, treated pine in Torquay's coastal environment requires regular maintenance to prevent the timber from drying, splitting and greying under harsh UV exposure. We recommend applying a quality timber preservative or semi-transparent stain every two to three years to maintain both the appearance and structural integrity of treated pine fencing in the Surf Coast region.

For Torquay homeowners willing to invest more upfront for superior longevity, hardwood options like treated hardwood, ironbark and spotted gum offer exceptional durability in coastal conditions. Treated hardwood combines the natural strength and density of Australian hardwoods with preservative treatment, providing a fence that can last 25 to 40 years with minimal maintenance. Ironbark is one of the most durable Australian timber species, naturally resistant to termites, rot and fire, it is classified as a BAL-29 rated timber, making it suitable for bushfire-prone areas around Torquay's western boundaries near the Otway foothills. Spotted gum offers a beautiful grain pattern and excellent durability, with natural oils that provide some resistance to moisture and UV damage. Hardwood fencing in Torquay typically costs $90 to $160 per linear metre installed, but the extended lifespan and reduced maintenance requirements often make it more cost-effective over the fence's lifetime compared to cheaper alternatives.

Colorbond fencing deserves consideration as an alternative to timber in Torquay, particularly for homeowners seeking maximum durability with minimal maintenance. Colorbond steel fencing is immune to termite damage, rot and UV degradation, and its pre-finished surface never requires painting or staining. In Torquay's coastal environment, Colorbond fences typically last 20 to 30 years with virtually no maintenance beyond occasional washing. The material is available in a wide range of colours that complement Torquay's coastal aesthetic, with popular choices including Classic Cream, Pale Eucalypt and Woodland Grey. Colorbond fencing in Torquay costs approximately $75 to $120 per linear metre installed for a standard 1800mm high fence. The main consideration for Torquay homeowners is that Colorbond can be noisy in strong winds, a factor worth considering for properties exposed to the Surf Coast's prevailing southerly winds. Some Torquay residents opt for a combination approach, using Colorbond for boundary fences and timber for decorative or feature fencing within their gardens.

Proper post installation is critical for fence longevity in Torquay, regardless of which material you choose. The Surf Coast's sandy soils and exposed position mean fences must be properly anchored to withstand strong wind loads. For timber posts in Torquay, we use a minimum of 600mm depth in the ground for a standard 1800mm fence, set in concrete footings that extend below the topsoil into the more stable clay or rock layer beneath. Posts should be spaced no more than 2400mm apart for optimal structural integrity, and all cut ends must be sealed with a preservative to prevent moisture ingress. In Torquay's coastal conditions, galvanised or stainless steel post stirrups and hardware are essential, standard zinc-plated fasteners can corrode rapidly in salt air, leading to premature fence failure. Fix Up Look Sharp uses only marine-grade or hot-dip galvanised hardware for all Torquay fencing projects, ensuring your fence remains structurally sound for decades to come.

Maintenance is the key to maximising your fence's lifespan in Torquay's demanding coastal environment. For timber fences, inspect annually for loose palings, damaged posts and signs of rot or insect activity, particularly at ground level where moisture contact is highest. Re-tension any wire stays on gates and check that all hinges and latches are secure and operating smoothly. Apply timber oil, stain or paint as needed to maintain the protective barrier against UV and moisture. In Torquay, we recommend a maintenance check every spring and autumn, coinciding with the periods of highest weather stress. For Colorbond fences, annual cleaning with fresh water and a soft brush will remove salt deposits and prevent staining. Check all post caps and panels for any damage from storms or impact. The cost of regular fence maintenance in Torquay is minimal compared to the expense of premature replacement, and a well-maintained fence significantly enhances your property's street appeal and overall value.

blogPosts.title: Preparing Your Torquay Rental Property for New Tenants: A Landlord's Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: A complete guide to preparing your Torquay rental property for new tenants. Covering maintenance, safety compliance, presentation and costs for Surf Coast landlords and property managers.
body: As a rental property owner in Torquay, ensuring your property is in top condition between tenancies is essential for attracting quality tenants and maximising your rental return. The Surf Coast rental market is competitive, with high demand from young professionals, families and seasonal workers, but tenants in this area have high expectations for property presentation and maintenance. At Fix Up Look Sharp, we work closely with Torquay property managers and private landlords to deliver comprehensive make-ready services that transform properties quickly and cost-effectively. Whether you manage a beachside unit near the Esplanade, a family home in Armstrong Creek or a holiday rental near Torquay's town centre, this guide covers the essential maintenance tasks that will ensure your property is presented at its best and ready for its next occupants.

The first impression of any rental property is the exterior, and in Torquay's coastal environment, outdoor areas require particular attention. Walk around the entire property and make a detailed list of all visible maintenance issues, cracked paths, peeling paint, damaged fences, overgrown gardens and dirty gutters are all common problems that immediately signal neglect to prospective tenants. Power washing driveways, paths and exterior walls can dramatically transform a property's appearance for minimal cost. Check that all exterior lighting is functional and replace any blown bulbs with energy-efficient LED options. Inspect the front door, house numbers and letterbox, these small details matter more than you might think when a prospective tenant first arrives for an inspection. In Torquay, where rental inspections are often scheduled back-to-back, a property with strong curb appeal will always attract more interest and potentially command a higher weekly rent from quality tenants.

Inside the property, focus on the areas that tenants notice first: walls, floors, bathrooms and kitchens. Filling and patching nail holes, scuffs and minor wall damage is inexpensive but makes an enormous difference to a property's presentation. A fresh coat of interior paint in a neutral colour like white, light grey or soft beige is the single most impactful improvement you can make between tenancies. In Torquay's rental market, we recommend using low-VOC paints that are environmentally friendly and safe for families. Pay special attention to the kitchen and bathroom, these rooms are deal-breakers for many tenants. Re-grouting tiles, replacing cracked or missing grout, re-siliconing around basins and showers, and ensuring all taps are drip-free are essential maintenance tasks. Check all cabinet doors and drawers for smooth operation, and replace any broken handles or hinges. These relatively small investments in Torquay rental properties typically deliver strong returns through reduced vacancy periods and higher rents.

The condition of flooring is one of the top three factors that influence a tenant's decision to apply for a rental property in Torquay. Carpet cleaning is a minimum requirement, but if the carpet is heavily stained, worn or dated, replacement may be more cost-effective than professional cleaning. Quality carpet replacement in Torquay typically costs $40 to $70 per square metre, installed with underlay. For hard flooring, check for any damaged tiles, scratched floorboards or lifting vinyl. Vinyl plank flooring has become extremely popular in Torquay rental properties due to its durability, water resistance and attractive wood-look appearance at a fraction of the cost of real timber. At $35 to $60 per square metre installed, quality vinyl plank can transform a tired-looking property into a modern, appealing home that attracts premium tenants. Do not forget to check and repair any squeaky floorboards, as these minor annoyances can become irritants for tenants over the duration of their lease.

Safety compliance is non-negotiable for Torquay rental property owners, and Victorian legislation requires specific standards to be met before a property can be leased. Smoke alarms must be installed in accordance with current regulations, this means photoelectric, interconnected alarms in every bedroom, hallway and living area. Check that all smoke alarms are within their serviceable life (typically 10 years from manufacture date) and test every unit to confirm proper operation. RCD safety switches must be installed at the switchboard and must protect all final sub-circuits. Ensure all power points, light switches and electrical fixtures are in good working order with no visible damage or exposed wiring. Handrails must be secure on all staircases and elevated areas. In Torquay, where many properties have elevated decks or are built on sloping blocks, checking balustrade compliance is particularly important. Fix Up Look Sharp can help Torquay landlords ensure their properties meet all current Victorian rental safety requirements.

Completing the make-ready process for your Torquay rental property involves a thorough final inspection to catch any remaining issues. Walk through every room with fresh eyes, as if you were seeing the property for the first time. Test every tap, flush every toilet, open and close every window and door, and check that all locks are functioning correctly. Ensure that all appliances provided with the property are clean and in working order, in Torquay's rental market, quality appliances are expected by tenants. Check that all wardrobe doors slide or open smoothly, that shelves are secure and that any internal lights are operational. Finally, arrange a professional clean of the entire property, including windows, to present it in pristine condition for photography and open inspections. The investment in a thorough make-ready typically pays for itself through faster tenant placement, higher rent and reduced ongoing maintenance issues throughout the tenancy period.
